rejected.title: Solving one-variable inequalities
card: An inequality uses <, >, ≤ or ≥. Solve it like an equation by doing the same thing to both sides.
One exception: when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, reverse the sign. So −2x < 6 gives x > −3.
The answer is a range of values, such as x > 3. On a number line, an open circle means the end value is not included (< or >), and a closed circle means it is included (≤ or ≥).
Example: 2x + 1 ≤ 9. Subtract 1: 2x ≤ 8. Divide by 2: x ≤ 4. Draw a closed circle at 4 with the line going left.
rejected.remember: Flip the sign if you multiply or divide by a negative. A closed circle includes the end value, an open one does not.

a.why: Add 2: 3x > 12. Divide by 3: x > 4. The answer x > 12 comes from forgetting to divide by 3, and x < 4 flips the sign even though 3 is positive.
a.clue: Undo the subtraction first, then undo the multiplication.

problems.detail: The why says x > 8 comes from forgetting to divide by 3 after adding 2. That is wrong: forgetting to divide gives 3x > 12, so x > 12. x > 8 would come from subtracting 2 instead of adding it (10 − 2 = 8) and then not dividing.

'Solve it like an equation: do the same thing to both sides' is given as the whole rule, and the remember line repeats it. It leaves out that the inequality sign reverses when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number. A student applying this rule to something like −2x < 6 would get the wrong answer.

final.title: Solving one-variable inequalities
card: An inequality uses \(<\), \(>\), \(\le\) or \(\ge\). Solve it like an equation by doing the same thing to both sides.
One exception: when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, reverse the sign. So \(-2x < 6\) gives \(x > -3\).

The answer is a range of values, such as \(x > 3\). On a number line, an open circle means the end value is not included (\(<\) or \(>\)), and a closed circle means it is included (\(\le\) or \(\ge\)).
Example: \(2x + 1 \le 9\). Subtract 1: \(2x \le 8\). Divide by 2: \(x \le 4\). Draw a closed circle at 4 with the line going left.
final.remember: Flip the sign if you multiply or divide by a negative. A closed circle includes the end value, an open one does not.
